title: Looped Plans settings
description: Everything the reader can change in Looped Plans, in one file. Generated from the app's own Settings type — do not edit by hand.

$schema.description: Where this file's schema lives. Written by Looped Plans, and rewritten on every launch so it always describes the build you are running.

monoId.description: The monospaced face used by the chrome and code blocks.

size.description: Body size in px, before the per-face optical correction.

leading.description: Line height as a multiple of the font size.

codeSize.description: Code block text size in px — code has its own conventions.

autosave.description: When edits reach disk, in the manner of an IDE: after a pause, when the window loses focus, or only on ⌘S.

diffExpandUnchanged.description: Show the whole file, or only the changed hunks with a little context.

diffLive.description: Re-diff as you type, versus only against what's saved on disk.

showExtensions.description: Filenames as they are on disk, extension and all.

showFrontmatter.description: Hold YAML frontmatter apart from the prose, above the page.

showCompleted.description: Whether finished plans stay in the tree. Off hides anything whose status reads as done, and anything inside a `completed/`-style folder — the two ways this app's own repository says a plan is over.

showAllFiles.description: Every text file in the tree, not only the markdown. Off is the default: a plans repository wants plans, not the machinery around them.

statuses.description: The choices the palette offers for `status:`, comma-separated. A convention, not a schema — a file may say anything; these are only what the app offers to write.

imageFolder.description: Where a pasted image is written, relative to the repository root.

sourceLineNumbers.description: Line numbers down the side of the raw markdown.

sourceWrap.description: Wrap long lines, or run them on and scroll sideways.

treeSize.description: Tree text size in px — ⌘+ / ⌘− while the tree has focus.

treeWidth.description: Sidebar width in px, dragged by its edge. Managed by Looped Plans — edit it here and the app will write over you.

agentCommand.description: The copyable agent command, as a template. `{prompt}` is the instruction, `{file}` the plan's repo-relative path. A template rather than a binary name because no two agents take a prompt the same way, and this app has no business preferring one.

chatCommand.description: Which agent from the catalogue the chat talks to. An id, not a command line. Every entry speaks ACP, so the argv is the app's business and what the agent can do is the agent's — there is nothing left here to configure but the choice.

handoffPrompt.description: The instruction "Hand off to agent: complete this plan" sends. Editable because it is the one piece of the feature that is about *your* house style, and a prompt you cannot see is a prompt you cannot argue with.

implementPrompt.description: The instruction "Hand off to agent: implement this plan" sends. Kept apart from the completion prompt because they ask for different moves: one writes the plan, the other builds from it.

rewritePrompt.description: The instruction "Rewrite…" sends for a selected passage. `{file}` is the file, `{quote}` the selected text, `{ask}` what you typed, and `{lines}` a line-range hint that is empty unless the quote is unique in the file.

chatScope.description: Whether `#` in the palette reaches the conversations of the repository you are in, or of every repository open. Per-repo by default, because a chat is usually about the plans next to it and a list that changes as you move between repositories is that list being right. "All" is for the other habit — one train of thought that outlives which window happens to be focused. A setting rather than a guess, because both are correct and which one you want is a fact about you.

treeSort.description: What orders the files in the tree. By name is the order a tree is read in, and the one to fall back to. By status is the cheap answer to wanting a plans folder sequenced some other way: the status is already read on every file during the walk, so it costs a comparison rather than a new field to maintain by hand — and unlike a number typed into every file, it cannot drift out of step with itself. Files with an unrecognised status, or none, come last either way.

showIndex.description: The file tree down the left.

showMux.description: The agent chat. Nothing runs while it is closed.

chatPlace.description: Where the chat sits: a column on the right, or a row under the document. Beside by default. A conversation is read down, so height is what it wants, and the plan stays fully visible next to it rather than being squeezed into the top half of the window.

muxHeight.description: Height of the chat in px, when it is the bottom row.

chatWidth.description: Width of the chat in px, when it is the right column.

watchSeconds.description: Poll interval for picking up outside edits, in seconds. 0 turns it off.

keyOverrides.description: Rebound shortcuts, by command id, merged over the registry's defaults the way this whole blob merges over `DEFAULTS`. "" means unbound. The shortcut sheet (⌘/) is the easy way in; the settings file is the other, and with a schema completing command ids it is a respectable one.

keyPreset.description: The preset keybinding pack merged between the registry's defaults and `keyOverrides` — personal rebinds survive switching packs. Strictly opt-in: "default" is the app's own bindings, untouched.

updates.description: Whether the app looks for a new version of itself. There is no "auto": replacing a running editor's binary without being asked is not a thing to do to someone who has unsaved text in it.

telemetry.description: Anonymous usage counts, so the app can be improved by something other than guesswork. Never file names, paths, or text. Off means nothing is sent.

lastSeenVersion.description: The version whose release notes have been shown. Anything older than what is running means the notes open once, by themselves, after an update. Managed by Looped Plans — edit it here and the app will write over you.
